title: Bunk on Jimmie Noone, Tio and knowing everyone's families
summary: Ralph Collins asks what Bunk said of Noone; Blumberg recalls generic praise and Russell Bunk knowing Noone's sister and everyone's relatives.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Yeah, go ahead, Ralph Collins is here to say something, go ahead.
Well, you mentioned a couple of reels back that he was, Bunk was talking about Jimmy Noon, and I wondered if you can remember anything that he said about Jimmy Noon.

I can't remember anything specific. I was asking him about all the clarinet players. Well, of course, at the time, I was caught up in the mythology of New Orleans music, and I was asking a lot of questions like, who was better, Jimmy Noon or Tio, you know? And of course, I realize now it's kind of a silly question in a way, you know, because they're all up there above a certain critical level. And so Bunk would, I guess, say, well, Tio played fine, and yeah, and of course Jimmy played fine, you know? And I mean, what else could he say? Of course, you know, that's the only, so that's the kind of answer I got on these kind of questions. Or he might have said something about, yeah, well, the last time I played with Jimmy was at so-and-so's place, you know, which I wouldn't have remembered five minutes later, you know, the place.
But he seemed to give the impression that he did play with Jimmy down here?

I don't remember. He sure gave the impression that he was familiar with Jimmy's playing, and that he, you know, considered him a fine clarinet player, one of the finest. I don't know where he might have run into Jimmy. I don't know.
We don't get too much information about him down here.

I remember vaguely something about Bunk and Jimmy going at the same, no, somebody, Jimmy Noon's sister, one of his sisters, probably not of too high a moral reputation, as they might say. I remember Bunk used to be her boyfriend and probably a dozen others. I do remember him talking about that, and he met this woman out in California, I believe, again, too. She was, Jimmy Noon's sister, was out in Oakland or something, in 1943 maybe, when they went out there. So Bunk at least had known the family. He knew everybody's family almost better than the people did.

That's right. He'd name relatives and cousins, and, and, uh, I understand when Louie brought a band that brought a big band into New York for some deal there, and Bunk was there, he was going, going through the whole band telling everybody about their uncles and their, their father, I knew your father, and they were all saying, yeah, that's right, that's right, yeah. One after the other. Of course, I wasn't there, that was just, that's all to me. Uh, I can't think of what.
